definition: In applied mathematics, branch and price is a method of combinatorial optimization for solving integer linear programming (ILP) and mixed integer linear programming (MILP) problems with many variables.
details: The method is a hybrid of branch and bound and column generation methods.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Think of it this way: In applied mathematics, branch and price is a method of combinatorial optimization for solving integer linear programming (ILP) and mixed integer linear programming (MILP) problems with many variables. And here is the clever part: The method is a hybrid of branch and bound and column generation methods. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Branch and price — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
